paragraphs: Combining several kinds of information only helps when their representations work together. This paper focuses on a weakness in multimodal learning: existing methods may not provide a clear indication that all participating modalities are aligned. A model can therefore fail to use information that should improve a downstream task.

TRIANGLE introduces a similarity measure based on the area of a triangle formed by three modality embeddings. It computes this geometric relationship directly in the space spanned by those representations. The measure replaces cosine similarity inside contrastive training objectives, giving training a way to improve the joint alignment of three modalities without adding fusion layers.

The authors evaluate the approach on three-modal tasks involving video-text retrieval, audio-text retrieval, and audio-video classification. They report state-of-the-art results across different datasets, with improvements over cosine-based methods reaching nine points of Recall@1. The contribution is both a training signal and an interpretable geometric account of alignment, connecting how representations relate to how effectively the model uses multiple sources of information.
neurips-2025-a-triangle-enables-multimod.tldr: TRIANGLE uses triangle-area similarity to jointly align three modalities, improving multimodal benchmarks without additional fusion layers.

paragraphs: This paper studies an attacker who corrupts a fraction of the training examples to cause failure on a particular test point. It addresses the agnostic setting, where learning does not assume that the available hypothesis class perfectly explains the data. The central question is how much additional error such targeted poisoning can force.

The authors establish that the optimal excess error scales as the square root of d times η, up to logarithmic factors. Here, d is the hypothesis class's VC dimension and η is the corrupted fraction. Achieving this rate requires randomized learners: the cited earlier result shows that deterministic learners can suffer error near one even with little poisoning. Surprisingly, the new upper bound still holds when the attacker sees the learner's random bits.

The lower bound also has a stronger form than a sample-size-specific impossibility result. A single fixed data distribution lets the attacker enforce the stated excess-error scale infinitely often. Together, the bounds characterize the achievable rate and show that randomness matters even without secrecy.
neurips-2025-agnostic-learning-under-tar.tldr: The paper establishes optimal agnostic learning rates under targeted poisoning and shows that randomized learners remain effective even when their randomness is visible.

paragraphs: DNA foundation models can represent genomic sequences effectively, but those representations do not by themselves provide multistep biological reasoning or understandable explanations. BioReason tackles this gap by tightly combining a DNA foundation model with a large language model. The language model can then interpret genomic information as part of its reasoning process.

The system is trained through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to produce deductions that are logical and biologically coherent. This connects sequence representation with explanations of biological predictions. The intended benefit is a model that can work through relationships in genomic information and present its decisions as a sequence of reasoning steps.

The authors report that accuracy on KEGG-based disease pathway prediction rises from 86% to 98%, alongside an average 15% improvement in variant effect prediction over strong baselines. They also report reasoning over biological entities not seen during training and step-by-step explanations. These findings support the approach as a way to combine improved predictive performance with more interpretable biological reasoning on the evaluated tasks.
neurips-2025-bioreason-incentivizing-mul.tldr: BioReason integrates a DNA model with an LLM to improve biological predictions and produce step-by-step explanations.

paragraphs: Federated continual learning must handle differences between clients while their tasks and data distributions also change over time. Sharing everything through a global model can introduce irrelevant knowledge and interfere with earlier learning. Fixed decentralized groups can also become ineffective when clients move to new tasks.

This paper proposes dynamic cooperative coalitions that produce personalized client models. Each client selectively joins others expected to improve its performance, creating non-overlapping groups that can change at each task stage. The framework estimates the benefit of cooperation using both the agreement between client gradients and the similarity of their models, connecting group formation to how compatible their learning currently is.

The authors represent these relationships through a coalitional affinity game and introduce merge-blocking and dynamic cooperative evolution algorithms to achieve cooperative and dynamic equilibrium. Experiments show improvements over various baselines. The approach makes the choice of collaborators part of continual learning itself, aiming to acquire useful new knowledge while retaining earlier learning as client relationships change.
neurips-2025-decentralized-dynamic-coope.tldr: Dynamic client coalitions enable selective knowledge sharing for personalized federated continual learning as tasks change.

paragraphs: Inverse protein folding starts with a desired three-dimensional protein structure and seeks an amino acid sequence that will fold into it. DualMPNN investigates whether structurally related proteins can provide useful guidance for this design problem. Its motivation comes from the importance of aligned sequences in protein structure prediction, transferred here to structural alignments for sequence design.

The model uses two interacting message-passing branches, one for the query protein and one for a structurally homologous template. Cross-stream attention takes the alignment into account when exchanging information. This allows the design process to combine geometric information with co-evolutionary signals from the template, making the relationship between the two proteins part of the model's computation.

On CATH 4.2, TS50, and T500, the authors report state-of-the-art sequence recovery rates of 65.51%, 70.99%, and 70.37%, respectively, exceeding ProteinMPNN. Analyses of template quality and structural foldability further support the usefulness of structural alignment priors. The findings indicate that aligned structural examples can substantially improve sequence recovery in the evaluated inverse-folding settings.
neurips-2025-dualmpnn-harnessing-structu.tldr: DualMPNN uses aligned structural templates through interacting neural branches to improve protein sequence design and benchmark recovery rates.

paragraphs: Spiking neural networks can use energy efficiently on neuromorphic hardware because their activations are sparse. Training them remains expensive: conventional surrogate-gradient training with backpropagation through time incurs computation and memory costs that grow linearly with the temporal dimension. This paper seeks strong performance when training resources are limited.

The proposed framework combines self-distillation with rate-based backpropagation. It projects firing rates from intermediate spiking layers into lightweight artificial neural network branches. Knowledge produced by the model then guides its own substructures through those branches, providing an additional pathway for optimization within the training framework.

A key observation is that the model's own teaching signals are not uniformly useful: low-quality signals can hinder convergence. The authors separate reliable and unreliable components and use only the reliable portion to guide learning. Experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, CIFAR10-DVS, and ImageNet demonstrate reduced training complexity alongside high performance. The contribution ties efficiency to selective self-teaching, rather than assuming every self-generated prediction is a helpful training target.
neurips-2025-enhanced-self-distillation-.tldr: The framework trains spiking networks efficiently by combining rate-based backpropagation with reliable self-distillation signals routed through lightweight ANN branches.

paragraphs: Diffusion language models can generate multiple tokens in parallel, offering a route to faster text generation. The paper identifies a problem with long decoding windows: tokens far from the input context can become repetitive or irrelevant. Dividing the window into semi-autoregressive blocks addresses this issue but sacrifices bidirectional processing and can also undermine speed through expanded time intervals.

Convolutional decoding narrows the decoding window through normalization without imposing hard block boundaries. This gives the model a more flexible way to control where generation happens while improving fluency. The authors pair it with Rejecting Rule-based Fine-Tuning, a post-training method designed to better align tokens at positions distant from the context.

The two methods address complementary parts of the same difficulty: how decoding is organized and how the model handles distant positions. On open-ended generation benchmarks including AlpacaEval, the authors report state-of-the-art performance among diffusion language model baselines, with significantly lower step size than previous work. Their findings demonstrate improvements in both generation quality and speed in these evaluations.
neurips-2025-fast-and-fluent-diffusion-l.tldr: Convolutional decoding and rejective fine-tuning improve diffusion language model fluency and speed by addressing generation far from the input context.

paragraphs: Generalized category discovery uses labeled examples from known categories to organize unlabeled data that may also contain unknown categories. This paper adds another difficulty: the unlabeled examples can come from unfamiliar domains as well. A system must therefore discover categories while handling distribution changes that can disrupt its clustering.

The proposed FREE framework uses frequency-domain information to address these shifts. It first separates samples into known and unknown domains according to differences in their amplitude components. It then exchanges amplitude components across domains to help adaptation and applies additional perturbations within the unknown domain to improve robustness to variation there.

FREE also extends the self-supervised contrastive objective and semantic clustering loss, and resamples data to give harder-to-cluster categories more attention. These elements connect domain adaptation with the actual difficulty of discovering categories. Across benchmark datasets, the authors report that the framework reduces the impact of distribution shifts and improves discovery of both known and unknown categories. The results support frequency information as a useful basis for category discovery when domain identity is also uncertain.
neurips-2025-generalized-category-discov.tldr: FREE uses frequency-based domain separation, perturbations, and adaptive resampling to improve category discovery under domain shifts.

paragraphs: The paper studies how to sample solutions of random, non-convex perceptron problems. Its setting is a high-dimensional limit where the numbers of examples and weights both grow while their ratio stays finite. Using replica theory, the authors develop a framework to predict the limits of efficient sampling with generative diffusion algorithms.

For a spherical perceptron with negative margin, the analysis finds efficient uniform sampling across most of the replica-symmetric region. Binary weights behave differently: uniform sampling remains intractable in the analysis. The authors conjecture that their predicted diffusion limits are attained when Approximate Message Passing supplies the score function, keeping this algorithmic optimality claim explicitly conjectural.

Investigating the binary obstruction leads to a potential, U(s) = −log(s), that makes a corresponding tilted distribution efficiently samplable by diffusion. This changes how solutions are weighted rather than establishing efficient uniform sampling for binary weights. Numerical experiments further show that annealing the potential's shape produces a fast, robust Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler for binary perceptron solutions.
neurips-2025-generative-diffusion-for-pe.tldr: A statistical-physics analysis predicts diffusion sampling limits for perceptrons and motivates an efficient sampler for a tilted binary solution distribution.

paragraphs: This paper considers minimizing a Lipschitz convex function when gradient information is noisy. Its key assumption concerns the shape of that noise: errors are bounded with high probability in every direction. The authors call this isotropic noise and investigate how this directional control can improve optimization complexity.

They develop an algorithm that improves on prior results by a factor equal to the dimension d in certain regimes. A consequence is a new state-of-the-art complexity for sub-exponential noise. Matching lower bounds, up to polylogarithmic factors, show that both results are close to the achievable limits under the analyzed conditions. The dimensional improvement is therefore tied to a specified noise setting and parameter regimes.

The paper also introduces a quantum isotropifier. This algorithm takes a quantum sampling oracle with bounded variance and converts it into one producing unbiased estimates with isotropic error. Combining that conversion with the optimization results yields improved dimension-dependent rates for quantum stochastic convex optimization. The quantum contribution makes the useful noise structure available from a different starting guarantee.
neurips-2025-isotropic-noise-in-stochast.tldr: Directional control of gradient noise enables near-optimal convex optimization improvements, with a quantum procedure extending the benefits to quantum sampling.

paragraphs: Multimodal knowledge graph completion predicts missing graph information using both relational structure and content associated with entities. That content can include text, images, or videos. The paper identifies several obstacles: entities have unequal information across modalities, different modalities describe the same entity differently, and their usefulness changes with the relational context.

LBMKGC uses CLIP to bring heterogeneous entity embeddings into better semantic alignment. It then combines those embeddings adaptively with guidance from the relation being considered. Distinguishing perceptual and conceptual attributes of triples helps determine how information should be fused, so the contribution of a modality can depend on the particular prediction.

This design addresses both compatibility between representations and variation in which evidence is useful. The authors compare LBMKGC with 21 state-of-the-art baselines and report superior performance across diverse datasets and scenarios while maintaining efficiency and generalizability. The findings support treating multimodal graph completion as context-dependent evidence combination, with semantic alignment and relational guidance working together to predict missing knowledge.
neurips-2025-lbmkgc-large-model-driven-b.tldr: LBMKGC combines CLIP-based semantic alignment with relation-guided multimodal fusion to improve knowledge graph completion.

paragraphs: Scientific work involves choosing experiments and interpreting their outcomes, often repeatedly as evidence accumulates. SciGym evaluates these abilities in language models through open-ended discovery tasks. It addresses the expense of biological wet-lab evaluation, where expertise, equipment, and time make repeated testing difficult.

The benchmark provides a computational dry lab built from biological system models encoded in Systems Biology Markup Language. These systems efficiently generate simulated data, allowing models to conduct iterative experimentation on realistically complex biological dynamics. The evaluation therefore centers on how a model designs experiments and analyzes results within a discovery process.

The authors evaluate six frontier language models on 137 small systems and release 350 systems in total. More capable models perform better, but every evaluated model deteriorates significantly as system complexity increases. This result identifies complexity as a substantial challenge even within the simulated setting. SciGym supplies a practical testbed for measuring progress on experimental reasoning, while its findings show considerable remaining room for improvement in scientific agents.
neurips-2025-measuring-scientific-capabi.tldr: SciGym tests iterative scientific discovery in simulated biological systems and finds that all six evaluated LLMs struggle increasingly as complexity grows.

paragraphs: Identifying molecular structures from mass spectra is difficult partly because annotated spectra are scarce. MS-BART addresses this by placing spectra and molecular structures into a shared token vocabulary. This supports large-scale pretraining on reliably computed fingerprint–molecule datasets, with denoising and translation objectives teaching the model complementary relationships between representations.

The pretrained system is adapted to experimental spectra using fingerprint predictions from MIST, a pretrained spectral inference model. This fine-tuning helps accommodate real spectral variability and reduces the distribution gap. However, the authors find that molecular hallucinations remain, so they add chemical feedback that steers generated molecules closer to reference structures.

The evaluations report state-of-the-art performance on five of twelve key metrics across MassSpecGym and NPLIB1. MS-BART is also faster by an order of magnitude than the competing diffusion-based methods, and ablation studies support its effectiveness and robustness. These findings present a combination of competitive structure elucidation and faster generation, with shared representation learning, experimental adaptation, and chemical feedback each contributing to the overall framework.
neurips-2025-ms-bart-unified-modeling-of.tldr: MS-BART combines shared spectrum–molecule tokens, pretraining, and chemical feedback, leading on five of twelve metrics while outperforming diffusion competitors in speed.

paragraphs: Parameter-efficient adaptation of language models can be disrupted by noisy training data. Cleaning that data can require substantial effort, while architectural approaches to handling noise can accumulate errors. LoPE explores a different training strategy: deliberately generated noisy data is used to improve the adaptation process's resistance to noise.

The framework combines asymmetric LoRA with an expert structure inspired by mixture-of-experts models. A dedicated poisoning expert receives noise injection during fine-tuning, developing its ability to discriminate and process noise. At inference, the system selectively masks this expert so that outputs draw on the purified knowledge acquired by the normal experts.

The training and inference stages therefore assign different roles to the noise-focused component. Exposure to generated noise shapes learning, while selective masking controls which experts contribute when producing an answer. Extensive experiments report strong performance and robustness using low-cost noise injection without requiring data cleaning. The stated result supports this method as a way to handle noisy adaptation data within the learning procedure itself.
neurips-2025-noise-robustness-through-no.tldr: LoPE trains a dedicated noise-processing LoRA expert and masks it at inference to improve robustness without data cleaning.

paragraphs: Image representations organized around objects can be compact and useful, but producing them through a segmentation model adds substantial cost. REN generates region representations directly from point prompts and patch-based image features. This bypasses the segmentation step used by approaches that combine systems such as SAM and DINO.

A lightweight module uses a few cross-attention blocks, with point prompts acting as queries and image features supplying keys and values. The resulting tokens correspond to the prompted objects. The authors train REN with DINO, DINOv2, and OpenCLIP, and show that it can extend to other encoders without dedicated training.

REN produces tokens 60 times faster with 35 times less memory while also improving token quality. In semantic segmentation and retrieval evaluations, it consistently improves on the original encoders in performance and compactness, and matches or exceeds SAM-based region approaches. It also reaches state-of-the-art results on Ego4D VQ2D and outperforms proprietary large multimodal models on Visual Haystacks' single-needle challenge. These results support direct region encoding as an efficient route to useful object-level representations.
neurips-2025-ren-fast-and-efficient-regi.tldr: REN directly converts point prompts and patch features into object-region tokens, improving quality while sharply reducing generation time and memory.

paragraphs: Concept bottleneck models predict labels through interpretable intermediate concepts. Their usefulness depends on learning the intended concepts, but correlations can cause a model to mix them up. Existing remedies can require statistically independent concepts or substantial annotation and intervention effort. This paper develops a framework that learns concepts with few labels and no interventions.

The method first uses unsupervised causal representation learning to extract latent causal variables from high-dimensional observations. It then learns a mapping from those variables to interpretable concepts. Separating these stages lets the framework use unlabeled observations for representation learning and reserve concept labels for aligning the representation with human-meaningful concepts.

The authors propose linear and non-parametric mappings with different guarantees. The linear estimator has a finite-sample, high-probability result, while the non-parametric estimator has asymptotic consistency. Synthetic and image benchmarks show less concept impurity and often better accuracy than other concept bottleneck models, including settings with strongly correlated concepts. The findings connect sample-efficient concept labeling with both theoretical guarantees and empirical improvements in concept quality.
neurips-2025-sample-efficient-learning-o.tldr: The framework aligns unsupervised causal representations with interpretable concepts using few labels, with theoretical guarantees and no interventions.

paragraphs: Mechanism design aims to make individual behavior serve collective objectives, but people or agents can differ in persistent traits such as skills and preferences. Learning a policy for such a system also requires accounting for complex interactions. When real-world interactions are costly, collecting enough experience becomes a central difficulty.

SWM-AP learns a social world model that represents behavior hierarchically. It infers agents' hidden traits from their interaction histories, then uses those traits to predict responses to deployed mechanisms. The mechanism policy obtains extensive training trajectories by interacting with this learned model, giving it additional experience for policy learning.

During real-world interactions, the method also updates its understanding of agent traits online. This connects predictions about heterogeneous behavior with continuing adaptation as experience arrives. Experiments in tax policy design, team coordination, and facility location show higher cumulative rewards and better sample efficiency than established model-based and model-free reinforcement learning baselines. The results support explicitly modeling persistent agent differences as a useful part of efficient mechanism-policy learning.
neurips-2025-social-world-model-augmente.tldr: SWM-AP infers agent traits and simulates their responses to train mechanism policies with better rewards and sample efficiency.

paragraphs: Knowledge distillation can improve spiking neural networks, but using a large external teacher or adding training machinery can be costly. This paper treats the outputs at different timesteps of one spiking network as separate submodels. Their output confidence provides an efficient way to identify stronger and weaker participants for self-distillation.

The authors explore two directions of teaching. Strong2Weak uses stronger timestep submodels to guide weaker ones. Weak2Strong reverses that direction, allowing weaker submodels to teach stronger ones through useful information described as dark knowledge. Both schemes support ensemble, simultaneous, and cascade implementations, providing several ways to organize the exchange.

Experiments show that the schemes improve the network's ability to distinguish inputs and its overall performance. Adversarial robustness also improves, which the authors associate with the stability introduced by self-distillation. The result is notable because useful supervision can flow in either direction between stronger and weaker submodels. It uses the temporal structure already present in spiking networks as a source of internal teaching signals.
neurips-2025-synergy-between-the-strong-.tldr: Spiking networks can self-distill across timesteps, with both strong-to-weak and weak-to-strong teaching improving performance and adversarial robustness.

paragraphs: Petrography examines thin sections of rock under polarization microscopes to identify minerals and understand rock properties. Expert visual analysis is labor-intensive, limiting how readily it can scale. This paper introduces LITHOS, a public experimental framework designed to support the development and evaluation of automated petrographic methods.

LITHOS contains 211,604 high-resolution RGB patches captured with polarized light and 105,802 expert-annotated grains spanning 25 mineral categories. Each grain annotation includes its mineral class, position, and expert-defined major and minor axes. These intersecting vector paths preserve information about grain geometry and orientation alongside the identification labels.

The authors evaluate multiple deep learning approaches and propose a dual-encoder transformer that combines both polarization modalities. It consistently outperforms models using a single polarization modality, supporting the value of combining the two views for mineral classification. By releasing the dataset, code, and pretrained models together, the paper provides both a substantial evaluation resource and a strong reference model for further research into automated analysis of rock thin sections.
neurips-2025-towards-automated-petrograp.tldr: LITHOS provides expert-annotated rock microscopy data and a dual-polarization transformer that improves mineral classification over single-polarization models.

paragraphs: A causal effect learned in one domain may change in another, especially when an unobserved factor influences the relationship between treatment and outcome. This paper studies transferring causal information when that hidden confounder cannot be measured directly. Instead, the available data include a proxy that provides indirect information about it.

The target domain presents a particularly sparse observation setting: only the proxy variable is observed there. The authors formulate the problem with discrete or categorical variables and prove that the target causal effect is identifiable under their conditions. They also state that identifiability extends to continuous treatment and response variables. Identifiability means the effect can be determined from the available information under the assumed setting.

Beyond identification, the paper introduces two estimation techniques, proves their consistency, and derives confidence intervals. Simulation studies and an application examining the effect of website rankings on consumer choices support the theory. The contribution connects a sparse-data transfer setting with statistical estimation and uncertainty assessment, showing how proxy information can support causal analysis across domains under the stated conditions.
neurips-2025-transferring-causal-effects.tldr: Under stated proxy and variable assumptions, the paper identifies and estimates target-domain causal effects when only the proxy is observed there.

paragraphs: A binary shadow mask records whether a location is shadowed but cannot express how strongly the shadow obscures the scene. This paper argues that this simplifies the interaction between light and objects too much. Details remain visible to varying degrees under both hard and soft shadows, motivating detection that also represents opacity.

The method first generates realistic training images with varied shadow opacity through an augmentation module. It then learns separate representations for shadow position and opacity. A prediction module combines these representations into a fine-grained opacity mask, making both where the shadow falls and how opaque it is part of the output.

The authors also construct a dataset with opacity-annotated shadow masks across varied scenarios. Experiments show qualitative and quantitative improvements over baselines, along with benefits for shadow removal, shadow editing, and three-dimensional reconstruction. The contribution changes the information supplied by shadow detection: downstream applications receive a graded description of the shadow, better reflecting the visible scene details that remain underneath it.
neurips-2025-under-the-shadow-exploiting.tldr: The paper predicts shadow opacity as well as location, improving fine-grained detection and downstream image and reconstruction tasks.

paragraphs: Differential privacy parameters can be difficult to translate into concrete statements about what an attacker might learn. This paper addresses three risks together: identifying a person, inferring an attribute, and reconstructing data. Existing translations can be inconsistent across attack settings and overly pessimistic when used to choose privacy noise.

Using the hypothesis-testing interpretation of differential privacy, called f-DP, the authors derive a common form of bounds on attack success across all three risks. These bounds are tunable with respect to baseline risk, including worst-case levels. That flexibility makes it possible to assess protection relative to the baseline risk relevant to a particular evaluation.

Empirically, the bounds are tighter than prior methods based on ε-DP, Rényi DP, and concentrated DP. Calibrating noise with the new bounds can reduce the required noise by 20% at the same risk level; one text classification example improves from 52% to 70% accuracy. The practical significance is a more consistent interpretation of privacy guarantees that can also improve utility when selecting noise.
neurips-2025-unifying-re-identification-.tldr: Unified f-DP attack-risk bounds make privacy guarantees easier to calibrate and can reduce noise while preserving the same assessed risk level.

paragraphs: Density estimation describes how probability is distributed across possible data values, making it central to generative modeling. Flexible neural methods can capture complex distributions but often provide limited interpretability and uncertainty quantification. Pólya trees offer a Bayesian nonparametric approach that represents distributional behavior over small intervals, although traditional inference can be computationally costly.

The variational Pólya tree replaces reliance on expensive sampling-based inference with stochastic variational inference for posterior computation. Its flexible Bayesian prior models latent densities and works with stochastic gradient optimization. This connects the Pólya tree framework to the optimization machinery used in deep learning, addressing a practical barrier to combining the two.

The model also uses the joint distribution likelihood to obtain a more precise variational posterior approximation than traditional mean-field methods. Evaluations on real data and images show competitive performance against state-of-the-art deep density estimators. The authors additionally explore interpretability and uncertainty quantification, positioning the method as a way to retain useful Bayesian structure while supporting scalable neural density modeling.
neurips-2025-variational-polya-tree-6848.tldr: Variational Pólya trees bring Bayesian nonparametric density modeling into stochastic-gradient training while exploring interpretability and uncertainty benefits.

paragraphs: Membership inference asks whether a particular example was used to train a model. For video understanding models, this could help assess whether sensitive recordings entered a training dataset. The paper finds that methods developed for text and images transfer poorly to video, especially when requiring few false positives or sampling more frames.

Vid-SME uses model-output confidence to calculate Sharma–Mittal entropy with adaptive parameterization for video inputs. It compares the entropy for a video in its natural temporal order with the entropy after reversing that order. The difference becomes a membership score, incorporating temporal variation into the assessment of whether the video appeared during training.

This design responds to two stated weaknesses of earlier approaches: overlooking changes across video frames and failing to account for model behavior as frame counts vary. Experiments on both self-trained and open-source video understanding models demonstrate strong effectiveness. The findings support temporal order and adaptive uncertainty measurement as useful signals for assessing video training membership in the evaluated models.
neurips-2025-vid-sme-membership-inferenc.tldr: Vid-SME estimates video training membership by comparing adaptive entropy scores for natural and temporally reversed frame sequences.

paragraphs: Audio source separation aims to recover individual sounds from a mixture. Supervised systems often need extensive labeled data tailored to the task and struggle with the variety of real acoustic scenes. ZeroSep investigates whether a pretrained text-guided audio diffusion model can perform separation without any task-specific training or fine-tuning.

The method first inverts the mixed recording into the diffusion model's latent space. It then uses text conditioning during denoising to guide recovery of individual sources. Under the right configuration, the model's existing generative capabilities support this separation task. Its textual priors also enable open-set scenarios, where the sounds of interest need not be confined to a fixed task-specific set.

The authors show compatibility with multiple pretrained text-guided audio diffusion backbones and strong results across several separation benchmarks, including performance above supervised methods. The zero-training claim concerns adaptation for separation: the approach still relies on a pretrained foundation model. Its main finding is that suitable inversion and text-guided denoising can repurpose that model for source recovery without additional task-specific learning.
neurips-2025-zerosep-separate-anything-i.tldr: ZeroSep repurposes pretrained text-guided audio diffusion models for source separation through inversion and denoising, without task-specific training.
